text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Namibian police has orderd the freezing of over N$700,000 in a private bank account of a man suspected of defrauding Namibia's transport parastatal TransNamib of about N$1 million.

- The Public Service Union of Namibia expressed disappointment at the government's intention to put salary adjustments for civil service due in April on hold until progress in downsizing the public sector has been made.
- The need to avert crippling strikes was underlined at an Alternative Dispute Resolution Workshop in Windhoek.

- There were sharp exchanges in parliament on Wednesday over the government's intention to amend the Local Authorities Act so that forthcoming local elections can be held on the basis of a party list system. Currently the Act stipulates that the war system must be used in local elections due in December.

- Employers have realised the urgent need to invest more time in improving labour relations after a strike by miners at TCL last year, a leading businessman told a workshop on industrial relations on Wednesday.
